claim: Serotonin (5-HT) neurons of the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) are positioned to enact coordinated modulation of circuits distributed across the entire brain through expansive innervation.
source: By means of an expansive innervation, the serotonin (5-HT) neurons of the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) are positioned to enact coordinated modulation of circuits distributed across the entire brain in order to adaptively regulate behavior.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that draws on established knowledge about DRN anatomy and function.

claim: The network computations that emerge from the excitability and connectivity features of the DRN are still poorly understood.
source: Yet the network computations that emerge from the excitability and connectivity features of the DRN are still poorly understood.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: A detailed electrophysiological characterization of genetically identified mouse 5-HT and somatostatin (SOM) neurons was carried out.
source: To gain insight into these computations, we began by carrying out a detailed electrophysiological characterization of genetically identified mouse 5-HT and somatostatin (SOM) neurons.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: A single-neuron modeling framework was developed that combines the realism of Hodgkin-Huxley models with the simplicity and predictive power of generalized integrate-and-fire models.
source: We next developed a single-neuron modeling framework that combines the realism of Hodgkin-Huxley models with the simplicity and predictive power of generalized integrate-and-fire models.
evidence: This describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: Feedforward inhibition of 5-HT neurons by heterogeneous SOM neurons implemented divisive inhibition.
source: We found that feedforward inhibition of 5-HT neurons by heterogeneous SOM neurons implemented divisive inhibition
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling simulations presented in the study.

claim: Endocannabinoid-mediated modulation of excitatory drive to the DRN increased the gain of 5-HT output.
source: while endocannabinoid-mediated modulation of excitatory drive to the DRN increased the gain of 5-HT output.
evidence: This is a finding from the modeling simulations presented in the study.

claim: The output of the DRN encodes a mixture of the intensity and temporal derivative of its input.
source: Our most striking finding was that the output of the DRN encodes a mixture of the intensity and temporal derivative of its input
evidence: This is a key finding from the modeling simulations presented in the study.

claim: The temporal derivative component dominates the DRN output mixture precisely when the input is increasing rapidly.
source: and that the temporal derivative component dominates this mixture precisely when the input is increasing rapidly.
evidence: This is a key finding from the modeling simulations presented in the study.

claim: The network computation of temporal derivative encoding primarily emerged from prominent adaptation mechanisms found in 5-HT neurons, including a previously undescribed dynamic threshold.
source: This network computation primarily emerged from prominent adaptation mechanisms found in 5-HT neurons, including a previously undescribed dynamic threshold.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the modeling simulations presented in the study.

claim: The DRN is particularly apt to encode input changes over short timescales.
source: By applying a bottom-up neural network modeling approach, our results suggest that the DRN is particularly apt to encode input changes over short timescales, reflecting one of the salient emerging computations that dominate its output to regulate behavior.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results presented in the study.

claim: DRN serotonin neurons have been proposed to modulate a wide range of cognitive processes.
source: DRN serotonin neurons have been proposed to modulate a wide range of cognitive processes, such as encouraging patience for future rewards (Miyazaki et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015), signaling the beneficialness of current actions or states (Luo et al., 2016), complementing reinforcement signals of dopamine (Daw et al., 2002; Maier and Watkins, 2005; Nakamura et al., 2008; Ranade and Mainen, 2009; Tops et al., 2009; Cools et al., 2011; Li et al., 2016), and, partially as a corollary, regulating both learning (Soubrié, 1986; Deakin, 1991; Daw et al., 2002; Dayan and Huys, 2009; Matias et al., 2017; Grossman et al., 2022) and mood (Savitz et al., 2009; Fava and Kendler, 2000; Donaldson et al., 2013; Cipriani et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: 5-HT neurons are organized into anatomical sub-modules that differentially regulate behavior.
source: For example, the unsuspected organization of 5-HT neurons into anatomical sub-modules that differentially regulate behavior (Abrams et al., 2004; Lowry et al., 2005; Commons, 2015; Muzerelle et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2018; Paquelet et al., 2022)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: 5-HT neurons can encode distinct salient features of the environment over different timescales.
source: or the observation that 5-HT neurons can encode distinct salient features of the environment over different timescales (Trulson and Jacobs, 1979; Schweimer and Ungless, 2010; Ranade and Mainen, 2009; Cohen et al., 2015; Zhong et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The slow firing rate (~5 Hz) of 5-HT neurons is in large part attributable to a large after-hyperpolarization potential (AHP).
source: For instance, the slow firing rate (~5 Hz) of 5-HT neurons, in large part attributable to a large after-hyperpolarization potential (AHP) (Aghajanian and Vandermaelen, 1982; Vandermaelen and Aghajanian, 1983)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Fast signaling despite slow firing can arise naturally in ensemble-rate codes.
source: However, fast signaling despite slow firing can arise naturally in ensemble-rate codes (Knight, 1972; Gerstner, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The in vivo population activity of 5-HT neurons has been observed to track impending rewards over second to sub-second timescales.
source: Consistent with this idea, the in vivo population activity of 5-HT neurons has been observed to track impending rewards over second to sub-second timescales (Zhong et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The trial-averaged ensemble rates of individual 5-HT neurons can track environmental changes over the millisecond timescale.
source: and the trial-averaged ensemble rates of individual 5-HT neurons can track environmental changes over the millisecond timescale (Ranade and Mainen, 2009; Cohen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: 5-HT receptor subtypes can regulate the excitability of target neurons over different timescales, including ionotropic 5-HT3 receptors with millisecond gating kinetics.
source: In addition, the fact that 5-HT receptor subtypes can regulate the excitability of target neurons over different timescales, including ionotropic 5-HT3 receptors with millisecond gating kinetics (Béïque et al., 2004; Béïque et al., 2007; Andrade, 2011; Varga et al., 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The most detailed single cell models of DRN neurons do not lend themselves with ease to bottom-up modeling efforts because of the substantial technical difficulty of obtaining sufficiently accurate values for a large number of interacting model parameters.
source: In spite of their conceptual utility, the most detailed single cell models, including those of DRN neurons (Tuckwell and Penington, 2014; Wong-Lin et al., 2011), do not lend themselves with ease to bottom-up modeling efforts because of the substantial technical difficulty of obtaining sufficiently accurate values for a large number of interacting model parameters (Prinz et al., 2004; Gerstner and Naud, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Generalized integrate-and-fire (GIF) models provide a strong foundation for network modeling because their small number of parameters can be estimated with a high degree of precision.
source: Mathematically simpler generalized integrate-and-fire (GIF) models provide a strong foundation for network modeling because their small number of parameters can be estimated with a high degree of precision (Mensi et al., 2012; Pozzorini et al., 2013; Teeter et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In the majority of the 5-HT neurons recorded, current steps induced strongly adapting action potential firing accompanied by large AHPs, and a characteristic kink in the voltage trace leading up to the first spike.
source: In keeping with previous descriptions (e.g. Vandermaelen and Aghajanian, 1983; Calizo et al., 2011), in the majority of the 5-HT neurons recorded in our dataset, current steps induced strongly adapting action potential firing accompanied by large AHPs, and a characteristic kink in the voltage trace leading up to the first spike (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1B and citations to prior literature.

claim: Qualitatively distinct firing patterns of 5-HT neurons were occasionally observed.
source: Qualitatively distinct firing patterns of 5-HT neurons were, however, occasionally observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Recordings from SOM neurons revealed spiking patterns that were more heterogeneous.
source: Recordings from SOM neurons revealed spiking patterns that were more heterogeneous (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SOM neurons were generally more sensitive to changes in input current (gain) than 5-HT neurons and responded to weaker inputs.
source: Comparing the relationship between the injected currents and firing frequencies between these populations, we found that SOM neurons were generally more sensitive to changes in input current (gain) than 5-HT neurons and responded to weaker inputs (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The gain showed greater variability in SOM neurons than in 5-HT neurons (Brown-Forsythe equality of variance test p=0.001 on N = 17 5-HT and N = 7 SOM neurons).
source: The gain showed greater variability in SOM neurons than in 5-HT neurons (Brown-Forsythe equality of variance test p=0.001 on N = 17 5-HT and N = 7 SOM neurons).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: In 5-HT cells, voltage steps revealed a large (peak amplitude 928 ± 249 pA, leak-subtracted), partly inactivating (steady-state amplitude 142 ± 45 pA, leak-subtracted) outward current.
source: In 5-HT cells, these experiments revealed a large (peak amplitude 928 ± 249 pA, leak-subtracted), partly inactivating (steady-state amplitude 142 ± 45 pA, leak-subtracted) outward current (Figure 1C1)
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1C1.

claim: The outward current in 5-HT cells was sensitive to Kv4-selective potassium channel blockers.
source: that was sensitive to Kv4-selective potassium channel blockers (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The gating and kinetic profile of the inactivating component of this conductance in 5-HT neurons are broadly similar to those expected of the A-type potassium currents (IA) characterized in great detail in several other cell types.
source: The gating and kinetic profile (Table 2, Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7) of the inactivating component of this conductance in 5-HT neurons are broadly similar to those expected of the A-type potassium currents (IA) characterized in great detail in several other cell types (e.g. Storm, 1989).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental observations to prior literature, with reference to Table 2, Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7, and a citation.

claim: An IA-like inactivating VGKC is a consistent feature of DRN 5-HT neurons.
source: Thus, an IA -like inactivating VGKC is a consistent feature of DRN 5-HT neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The same voltage-clamp protocol applied to SOM neurons triggered a mixture of outward and inward currents that varied widely from cell to cell.
source: The same voltage-clamp protocol applied to SOM neurons, in contrast, triggered a mixture of outward and inward currents that varied widely from cell to cell (Figure 1D2).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1D2.

claim: A significant proportion of SOM neurons did not express a transient outward current at all (27.3 %).
source: A significant proportion of SOM neurons did not express a transient outward current at all (27.3 %, Figure 1E)
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: The expression of this subthreshold voltage-gated current is substantially more variable in SOM neurons than in 5-HT neurons.
source: Together, these results show that the expression of this subthreshold voltage-gated current is substantially more variable in SOM neurons than in 5-HT neurons, in line with the distinctive heterogeneity of excitability features observed in this DRN cell type (Figure 1C2, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations, with reference to Figure 1C2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: IA introduced a kink in the subthreshold voltage leading up to spike threshold in a toy leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) model.
source: In keeping with previous studies, IA introduced a kink in the subthreshold voltage leading up to spike threshold (Getting, 1983; Segal, 1985; McCormick, 1991; Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 2A and citations to prior literature.

claim: IA increased the latency to the first spike evoked by a square step stimulus, particularly when starting from a hyperpolarized voltage at which IA is free from inactivation.
source: and increased the latency to the first spike evoked by a square step stimulus, particularly when starting from a hyperpolarized voltage at which IA is free from inactivation (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 2B and C.

claim: The predicted relationship between initial voltage and latency was experimentally recapitulated in whole-cell recordings from identified 5-HT neurons.
source: The predicted relationship between initial voltage and latency was experimentally recapitulated in whole-cell recordings from identified 5-HT neurons (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 2D–F.

claim: The onset of spiking was delayed by hyperpolarization.
source: In particular, the onset of spiking was delayed by hyperpolarization (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The magnitude of the effect of hyperpolarization on spike onset was significantly reduced by the partial pharmacological block of IA with 4-AP (p=3.2e-6 for initial voltages between –90 mV and –70 mV).
source: and the magnitude of this effect was significantly reduced by the partial pharmacological block of IA with 4-AP ( p=3.2e-6 for initial voltages between –90 mV and –70 mV; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data, with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: An inflection point predicted by the model was observed in the normalized initial-voltage/latency relationship.
source: Finally, we also observed an inflection point predicted by the model in the normalized initial-voltage/latency relationship (Figure 2F, compare with model prediction in Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations, with reference to Figure 2F and Figure 2C.

claim: IA causes an increase in spike latency and jitter in the presence of noise in simulated populations of toy neurons.
source: Whereas subthreshold fluctuations yielded time-locked spikes without IA (Figure 2G), they induced spiking with larger jitter across the simulated population when IA was present (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 2G and Figure 2H.

claim: The desynchronizing effect of IA decreased the peak population rate at the time corresponding to the mean latency.
source: This desynchronizing effect of IA also decreased the peak population rate at the time corresponding to the mean latency (Figure 2I)
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 2I.

claim: IA may regulate the gain of the DRN network to time-varying inputs.
source: Taken together, results from these toy models revealed a role of IA in regulating the degree of synchronization of a population following sudden inputs, suggesting that IA may regulate the gain of the DRN network to time-varying inputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: 5-HT neurons were distinguishable from SOM and mPFC cells by their long membrane time constants.
source: 5-HT neurons were distinguishable from SOM and mPFC cells by their long membrane time constants (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 5-HT neurons were distinguishable from SOM and mPFC cells by the presence of conspicuously potent and protracted adaptation mechanisms.
source: and by the presence of conspicuously potent and protracted adaptation mechanisms (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 4B–D.

claim: In addition to evoking a characteristically large and prolonged adaptation current, action potential firing in 5-HT neurons produced a substantial and long-lasting increase in firing threshold.
source: Indeed, in addition to evoking a characteristically large and prolonged adaptation current (Figure 4C), action potential firing in 5-HT neurons produced a substantial and long-lasting increase in firing threshold (Figure 4D; but note that this effect is somewhat attenuated near physiological temperature, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 4C, Figure 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: SOM neurons most often displayed either negligible or even depolarizing spike-triggered currents that may underlie the burst firing patterns often observed in this cell type.
source: In contrast, SOM neurons most often displayed either negligible or even depolarizing spike-triggered currents (Figure 4B and C) that may underlie the burst firing patterns often observed in this cell type (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 4B, Figure 4C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: 5-HT neurons are characterized by slow membrane dynamics, IA, and particularly prominent adaptation mechanisms.
source: Thus, 5-HT neurons are characterized by slow membrane dynamics, IA, and particularly prominent adaptation mechanisms.
evidence: This is a summary of the modeling results.

claim: The population firing rates of 5-HT, SOM, and mPFC neurons transiently increased before relaxing to a significantly lower stationary level in response to step increases of synaptic-like inputs.
source: In response to step increases of synaptic-like inputs delivered to the entire population (Figure 5B left), the population firing rates (in Hz/neuron; Figure 5B right) of 5-HT, SOM, and mPFC neurons (Figure 5C) transiently increased before relaxing to a significantly lower stationary level.
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 5C.

claim: The transient and stationary parts of the population input-output functions were approximately rectified linear functions.
source: The transient and stationary parts of the population input-output functions were approximately rectified linear functions (Figure 5—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: While the gain of the transient response was greater than that of the stationary response in all three cell types, the ratio of transient to stationary gain was substantially higher in 5-HT neurons (ratio of 3.42 ± 0.07 vs. 1.89 ± 0.04 in SOM and 1.50 ± 0.03 in mPFC; p<0.001 in each case).
source: While the gain of the transient response was greater than that of the stationary response in all three cell types, the ratio of transient to stationary gain was substantially higher in 5-HT neurons (Figure 5E; ratio of 3.42 ± 0.07 vs. 1.89 ± 0.04 in SOM and 1.50 ± 0.03 in mPFC; p<0.001 in each case; but note that the gain ratio in 5-HT neurons falls to 2.13 ± 0.03 near physiological temperature [Figure 5—figure supplement 5], consistent with a smaller spike-triggered threshold movement [Figure 4—figure supplement 2]).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of modeling results, with reference to Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 5, and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The marked response of 5-HT cells occurred quickly, in the first 100 ms after the onset of the step.
source: This marked response of 5-HT cells occurred quickly, in the first 100 ms after the onset of the step.
evidence: This is a description of modeling results.

claim: Despite 5-HT neurons being characterized by slow membrane time constants, their population activity provided a remarkably strong encoding of the onset of step synaptic inputs.
source: Thus, despite 5-HT neurons being characterized by slow membrane time constants, their population activity provided a remarkably strong encoding of the onset of step synaptic inputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: The characteristically strong spike-triggered adaptation of 5-HT neurons contributed to the observed relaxation of the population response to a lower stationary level.
source: We found that the characteristically strong spike-triggered adaptation of 5-HT neurons (spike-triggered hyperpolarizing adaptation current and threshold movement shown in Figure 4) contributed to the observed relaxation of the population response to a lower stationary level: grafting the weak adaptation from SOM neuron models onto 5-HT models dramatically reduced the ratio of transient to stationary gain, and vice-versa (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 4 and Figure 5F.

claim: The preferential sensitivity of 5-HT neuron populations to sudden changes in synaptic inputs is a natural consequence of strong adaptation at the single neuron level.
source: Therefore the preferential sensitivity of 5-HT neuron populations to sudden changes in synaptic inputs is a natural consequence of strong adaptation at the single neuron level.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: The gain of the transient component of the 5-HT response increased markedly when the conductance of IA was set to zero.
source: The gain of the transient component of the 5-HT response increased markedly when the conductance of IA was set to zero (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: Increasing the potency of IA substantially dampened and broadened the population response to fast inputs.
source: while increasing the potency of IA substantially dampened and broadened the population response to fast inputs, reminiscent of IA's modulation of spike timing jitter observed in our toy model (Figure 2I–K).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 2I–K.

claim: IA substantially regulates the gain of the transient component of DRN 5-HT output evoked by sustained inputs, with negligible effects on the gain of the slower stationary component.
source: These simulations thus show that IA substantially regulates the gain of the transient component of DRN 5-HT output evoked by sustained inputs, with negligible effects on the gain of the slower stationary component.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: Including FFI onto 5-HT neurons substantially dampened the overall response of the 5-HT population to synaptic inputs, while still sustaining the preferential encoding of the early phase of sudden inputs.
source: Including FFI onto 5-HT neurons substantially dampened the overall response of the 5-HT population to synaptic inputs, while still sustaining the preferential encoding of the early phase of sudden inputs (Figure 6B2).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 6B2.

claim: Simulating the effects of endocannabinoid modulation of excitatory input to the DRN by weakening the strength of the input to SOM neuron populations by 30% led to an increase in the overall gain of the DRN that was apparent across the entire duration of the response to step inputs.
source: We next directly simulated the effects of endocannabinoid modulation of excitatory input to the DRN observed experimentally (Geddes et al., 2016) by weakening the strength of the input to SOM neuron populations by 30% while leaving that to 5-HT neurons intact. By favoring the direct monosynaptic excitation of 5-HT neurons by preferentially diminishing the glutamatergic drive of SOM neurons, this neuromodulation led to an increase in the overall gain of the DRN that was unexpectedly apparent across the entire duration of the response to step inputs (i.e. no change in the gain ratio, Figure 6B2).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 6B2 and a citation to prior literature.

claim: The target-specific endocannabinoid-mediated modulation of PFC excitatory drive in DRN exerts a normalizing role by increasing the overall gain of 5-HT output evoked by synaptic inputs without altering its preferential encoding of changes in input.
source: Thus, the target-specific endocannabinoid-mediated modulation of PFC excitatory drive in DRN exerts a normalizing role by increasing the overall gain of 5-HT output evoked by synaptic inputs without altering its preferential encoding of changes in input, which is emerging as a cardinal feature of DRN network dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: FFI with an experimentally determined degree of heterogeneity mainly imposed a reduction of the slope of the input-output function (i.e. divisive inhibition), while homogeneous FFI mainly shifted the input-output function of the transient component of the population response to the right (i.e. subtractive inhibition).
source: Thus, while FFI with an experimentally determined degree of heterogeneity mainly imposed a reduction of the slope of the input-output function (i.e. divisive inhibition), homogeneous FFI mainly shifted the input-output function of the transient component of the population response to the right (i.e. subtractive inhibition; Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: Heterogeneity among GABAergic neurons implements divisive inhibition.
source: Therefore, we conclude that heterogeneity among GABAergic neurons implements divisive inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: The peak 5-HT neuron population firing rate linearly reported the slope of the ramps, an effect which was enhanced by FFI.
source: Remarkably, the peak 5-HT neuron population firing rate linearly reported the slope of the ramps, an effect which was enhanced by FFI (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: The linearity of the peak 5-HT neuron population firing rate encoding the slope of the ramps was conditional on the presence of slightly depolarizing background input (≥20 pA).
source: We further found that this linearity was conditional on the presence of slightly depolarizing background input (≥20 pA, Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 7D.

claim: The potent adaptation mechanisms of 5-HT neurons play a key role in mediating the linear encoding of input derivative, since reducing the strength of adaptation reduces linearity across a wide range of input baselines.
source: The potent adaptation mechanisms of 5-HT neurons play a key role in mediating this linear encoding of input derivative, since reducing the strength of adaptation reduces linearity across a wide range of input baselines (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 7E and Figure 7F.

claim: The DRN signals to its brain-wide target a mixture of the intensity and temporal-derivative of its excitatory inputs, and the derivative-encoding component dominates when the input is increasing rapidly.
source: Together, these observations suggest that the DRN signals to its brain-wide target a mixture of the intensity and temporal-derivative of its excitatory inputs, and that the derivative-encoding component dominates when the input is increasing rapidly (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Removing IA from 5-HT neurons in DRN network models extended the range of background input where the peak 5-HT neuron population firing rate is an approximately linear function of the slope of a ramp stimulus.
source: Consistent with this idea, removing IA from 5-HT neurons in our DRN network models extended the range of background input where the peak 5-HT neuron population firing rate is an approximately linear function of the slope of a ramp stimulus (Figure 7E and G).
evidence: This is a description of modeling results, with reference to Figure 7E and Figure 7G.

claim: The presence of strong spike-frequency adaptation in 5-HT neurons causes the DRN to signal the rate of change of its input to its brainwide targets, but this core computation is progressively suppressed when a state of hyperpolarization engages IA.
source: In summary, we found that the presence of strong spike-frequency adaptation in 5-HT neurons causes the DRN to signal the rate of change of its input to its brainwide targets, but that this core computation is progressively suppressed when a state of hyperpolarization engages IA .
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: 5-HT neurons were relatively homogeneous and characterized by potent spike-frequency adaptation and by the presence of a strong A-type potassium current.
source: Consistent with, and extending, previous work, we found that 5-HT neurons were relatively homogeneous and characterized by potent spike-frequency adaptation (Figure 1) and by the presence of a strong A-type potassium current (Figure 2)
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 1 and Figure 2.

claim: SOM neurons displayed a considerably more heterogeneous excitability profile.
source: while SOM neurons displayed a considerably more heterogeneous excitability profile (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings, with reference to Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Extensions to classical GIF models to capture the non-linear subthreshold effects of IA observed in 5-HT neurons were required to adequately capture the spiking response of 5-HT neurons to naturalistic stimuli.
source: Extensions to classical GIF models (Mensi et al., 2012; Pozzorini et al., 2015) to capture the non-linear subthreshold effects of IA observed in 5-HT neurons were required to adequately capture the spiking response of 5-HT neurons to naturalistic stimuli (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 3 and citations to prior literature.

claim: The substantial spike-frequency adaptation observed in 5-HT neurons is not fully explained by their distinctively large AHPs and is partly mediated by a previously undescribed dynamic spike threshold.
source: Inspecting the parameters of the best performing GIF models revealed that the substantial spike-frequency adaptation observed in 5-HT neurons is not fully explained by their distinctively large AHPs and is partly mediated by a previously undescribed dynamic spike threshold (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 4.

claim: The prominent adaptation mechanisms in 5-HT neurons regulated DRN population responses to synaptic inputs.
source: Thus, we found that the prominent adaptation mechanisms in 5-HT neurons regulated DRN population responses to synaptic inputs (Figure 5)
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 5.

claim: IA suppressed the response to sudden inputs.
source: that IA suppressed the response to sudden inputs
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings.

claim: Heterogenous FFI had a divisive rather than subtractive effect on DRN output.
source: and that heterogenous FFI had a divisive rather than subtractive effect on DRN output (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 6.

claim: 5-HT neurons linearly reported a mixture of the intensity and temporal-derivative of their synaptic inputs.
source: By further exploring DRN population dynamics, our simulations demonstrated that 5-HT neurons linearly reported a mixture of the intensity and temporal-derivative of their synaptic inputs (Figure 7)
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 7.

claim: The temporal-derivative dominates DRN output when the input is increasing rapidly.
source: and that the temporal-derivative dominates DRN output when the input is increasing rapidly (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a summary of modeling findings, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 'augmented GIF' model developed here explicitly incorporates the most important biophysical features of 5-HT neurons, allowing us to probe their contributions to network-level computation by altering or removing the corresponding model components during network simulations.
source: Preserving the accuracy and identifiability of simpler approaches (Gerstner and Naud, 2009; Mensi et al., 2012; Pozzorini et al., 2013; Teeter et al., 2018), the 'augmented GIF' model developed here explicitly incorporates the most important biophysical features of 5-HT neurons, allowing us to probe their contributions to network-level computation by altering or removing the corresponding model components during network simulations.
evidence: This is a description of the methodological contribution of the study, with citations to prior literature.

claim: The effect of IA on spike latency depends at least to some extent on its effective magnitude and inactivation kinetics.
source: The effect of IA on spike latency depends at least to some extent on its effective magnitude and inactivation kinetics (defined as the ratio of maximal A-type conductance to inverse membrane resistance and the ratio of the inactivation time constant of IA to the membrane time constant; see Methods).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: The AHPs of 5-HT neurons do not reach the hyperpolarized potentials required to free IA from inactivation.
source: This discrepancy can be explained by noting that the AHPs of 5-HT neurons (and thus of our computational model) do not reach the hyperpolarized potentials required to free IA from inactivation (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1), in contrast to the model of Connor et al., 1977.
evidence: This is an explanation of a discrepancy between the current findings and prior literature, with reference to Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and a citation.

claim: As a result, IA remains mostly inactivated during sustained inputs, and the stationary response is mostly regulated by the interplay between spike-triggered adaptation and the strength of the input.
source: As a result, IA remains mostly inactivated during sustained inputs, and the stationary response is mostly regulated by the interplay between spike-triggered adaptation and the strength of the input.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.
